text:
Nothing separated these teams for 65 minutes, and a six-round shootout only confirmed it. Zachary Bolduc scored the lone goal of the night in the sixth round, after Cole Caufield, Alexandre Texier, Juraj Slafkovský, Nick Suzuki and Lane Hutson had all been stopped for MTL, and after Lucas Raymond, Alex DeBrincat, Viktor Arvidsson, Dylan Larkin and Axel Sandin-Pellikka had been stopped for DET. Nate Danielson then failed to answer, and MTL took it 1-0.

The game itself had no goals, and the numbers say it could have gone either way. Each team put 30 shots on goal, and the expected goals finished at 3.60 for MTL and 3.57 for DET, which leaves both at a 50 percent chance of deserving the win. MTL controlled more of the puck, with 76 shot attempts to 53, and held the even-strength edge in chance quality, 2.57 expected goals to 1.98. But DET blocked 22 shots to MTL's 12, and neither side cashed in on four power plays. DET's 1.59 expected goals on the man advantage were the biggest swing it failed to turn into a goal.

Both goalies were the story. Jacob Fowler stopped all 30 shots against an expected 3.57 goals, and Daniil Tarasov matched him, saving 3.6 goals more than his shots deserved. DeBrincat was the closest DET came to breaking through, putting seven shots on goal and missing the net on a 46 percent look in the second period. Fowler was named the first star for MTL, with Tarasov second.
